The setup has nine steps for restaurant and experience businesses, or eight for professional services, which skips the products step. ChatGPT is optional and connects after the site exists.
Before you startSign in to your KrabiClaw account, then open onboarding.
Have your business name, street address, city, country, business contact number, currency, and homepage headline ready. You can also add opening hours, a logo, a brand color, and a real business photo.
Completed steps save your progress as a private draft. Use Save & exit to leave the flow, then return to onboarding to resume from your saved answers. Use Next to save the current step before leaving; do not assume an unfinished field has been saved. Saving a draft does not publish your site.
1. Choose your business typeChoose Restaurant, café or bar; Experience or activity; or Professional services. This determines which setup steps and starting content apply to your business.
2. Find your business or enter it manuallyType your business name in the Google Maps search picker and choose the correct listing. Selecting the listing brings available address, phone, and hours into the following screens, where you can check and change them.
If you cannot find the right listing, type your business name and choose Enter details manually. You do not need to paste a Google Maps URL or connect Google Analytics to use this step.
3. Check the addressReview or enter the street address, city, and country. These are required to continue. Complete any other address fields that apply, and make sure customers will be directed to the right place.
4. Add the business contact numberEnter the number customers should use to contact the business. A business contact number is required. Notification preferences are configured separately; this is not a manager alert-number setup screen.
5. Add hours, or continue without themCheck the timezone and opening hours, including any exceptions you know about. When the country has one timezone, it may be proposed for you; verify it rather than assuming it is right.
Hours are an optional setup step. If you skip them, add accurate hours before relying on the site to tell customers when to visit.
6. Choose your currencyConfirm the currency you charge in. The country may suggest a currency; choose another if needed. A currency is required before continuing, including for professional services.
7. Add your first offerings, if applicableRestaurant and experience businesses can add initial menu items or offerings. This step is optional, so you can continue and add them later. Professional services skips this step entirely.
Only enter real names and prices. Adding an offering here does not by itself verify a complete customer booking or payment flow.
8. Set the homepage headline and lookEnter the required Hero headline: a clear statement of what your business offers. You can also add a Hero description.
Brand color, Logo, and Hero photo are optional. Choose a color swatch or custom color, upload a logo, and upload your own hero photo if you have them ready. Wait for uploads to finish and check the preview. Unlike the optional images and color, the headline cannot be left blank.
9. Review, then choose Create my siteReview the site preview and your answers. Use Back to correct details before continuing. A private preview is for review; it is not proof that the public site is live.
When you are ready, choose Create my site. This is the explicit activation step. Wait for it to succeed and for KrabiClaw to open the site dashboard. If an error appears, read it and correct the problem rather than assuming creation finished.
Check the public resultOpen the site's public address from the dashboard. Then check it in a private browser window without a preview token or signed-in preview session.

The site opens as a customer would see it
The business name, headline, address, phone, and hours are accurate
Any displayed offerings and prices are correct
The main button leads to the intended page, phone number, or customer action
Photos and text look usable on a phone as well as a larger screen

Do these checks before sharing the address. A working preview and a working public site are different checks.
TroubleshootingThe Google Maps picker does not find my business. Try its business name and location, choose only the correct listing, or use Enter details manually.
Next is disabled. Check the current required answer: business choice/name, street address/city/country, business contact number, currency, or Hero headline. Optional hours and offerings do not block the flow.
I left before finishing. Return to onboarding with the same account. It restores saved progress and takes you to the first unanswered required step, or review if those answers are complete.
Creation returned an error. Keep the saved draft and address the displayed error. Check the dashboard for an existing site before starting another setup.
Next stepNext, make your first site edit and verify it on the public site. You can also customize your brand and theme, or connect ChatGPT if you prefer conversational edits.

You need an existing KrabiClaw site and permission to edit its content. If you have not created a site yet, follow Create and publish your first site.
1. Choose the exact destinationIn the dashboard, select your business and open the page you want to change. Check the page title, public path and language before editing. If the content belongs to a branch, confirm that location too.
With a connected assistant, first ask it to identify your business and read the current page. A business name or URL helps identify the site, but the assistant must resolve it to the accessible organization rather than guess an internal ID.
2. Make one specific changeIn the page editor, change only the intended text and save. Treat changes to an existing live page as customer-facing; do not assume the draft-and-publish workflow for articles also applies to page edits.
For an assistant edit, provide the exact replacement and ask it to preserve the page path, language, other blocks and media. For a single paragraph, a targeted block edit avoids replacing the whole page. If the page changed since it was read, the assistant should read it again before saving.
Try with your connected assistantReplace the example business, page and details with your own.Change one paragraphCopy promptOn my Harbor Studio site, read the English About page and show me its current opening paragraph. Replace only that paragraph with: “We offer small-group creative workshops for adults.” Keep the page URL, other text and media unchanged. Then read the page back and give me its public link.3. Check the resultOpen the public page, not just the editor. Check the new words on both a narrow and a wide screen. Follow any link you changed. Ask the assistant to read back the saved text as a second check; a successful save alone does not prove the public layout looks right.
If the old text remains, confirm the business, page and language, then reload the public page. If a save conflicts with another edit, inspect the latest version instead of repeatedly overwriting it. To undo your wording change, restore the original sentence after checking for newer edits.
Keep the task smallCreating sites and locations, Google Places lookup and domain setup happen in the dashboard. Connected assistants manage existing-site content; they do not replace those setup flows.Next: Customize your brand and theme.

A post is different from a long-form blog article or a permanent site page. You can publish to your website, a connected Facebook Page, a connected Instagram professional account, or an explicit combination.
1. Check the destinationsChoose the correct business and, if relevant, location. Check the exact connected Page or account name and any reported connection or plan problem. Connect or change social accounts in the dashboard using the Facebook or Instagram guide.
Importing existing social posts is separate from publishing a new one. A working import is not evidence that this draft has been published.
2. Draft and previewPrepare the caption, optional title, call-to-action link and media in order. Open the draft preview and check spelling, dates, link destinations and media. Uploaded media has a public delivery URL even while the post is a draft.
Facebook accepts text, a link, photos or one video. Instagram accepts one JPEG image, a carousel of up to ten items, or one video as a Reel; its call to action appears as text. Check the current destination requirements before approving the post.
Try with your connected assistantReplace the example business, page and details with your own.Prepare a website-only draftCopy promptCreate a draft post for Harbor Studio: “Our autumn workshop dates are now available.” Use no media or call to action. Show me the preview and the available publishing destinations. Do not publish yet.3. Approve exact targetsName each destination you want. For example: “Publish this draft to the Harbor Studio website and the connected Facebook Page named Harbor Studio, but not Instagram.” Website publication is a separate target; publishing to a social account does not mean you also chose the website.
KrabiClaw does not provide native scheduled publication. A draft remains a draft until a publish action happens; a request to prepare something for later is not a scheduled job.
4. Check every resultAsk for an outcome and public link for each target. Published or already published confirms that destination. Other outcomes need attention:

Processing: the provider is still preparing media. Continue the same post's publish operation rather than create another post.
Unknown: reconcile the existing publication with the provider. Do not publish again or make a duplicate to resolve uncertainty.
Failed or skipped: read the reason and fix that destination's issue before retrying. Keep successful destinations intact.

Open the returned public links to verify the content. If no link is available, report that limitation instead of treating a missing URL as proof of failure.
Changes after publicationEditing a published post changes the website copy only. It does not edit the Facebook or Instagram copies. Deleting it from KrabiClaw removes the website post, not the external social posts.Next: Read your site analytics.

Create your first site in the KrabiClaw dashboard before using the connection to edit it.
Choose the setup route you have
There are two different flows. Follow the one available to your account:

Personal plugin during the approval period: use the KrabiClaw listing or installation route provided to you. If you already installed it and new tools are missing, follow Get the latest KrabiClaw tools in ChatGPT. That guide documents the Personal-plugin flow tested in September 2026, including its desktop/tablet browser reinstall step.
Custom MCP app using Developer mode: follow the developer connection steps below when your account or workspace permits this route.

The Personal listing is not guaranteed to appear for every account. Creating a custom MCP app and installing a Personal plugin are different operations; do not assume their menus or mobile availability are the same.
Developer connection
Use ChatGPT in a web browser. Developer-mode access and app creation depend on your ChatGPT plan and workspace permissions. Check OpenAI's current developer-mode instructions if a control is missing.
1. Open the custom-app controls
Open ChatGPT's Apps settings and find the custom-app creation controls. Depending on your workspace, Developer mode is enabled through Apps → Advanced Settings or workspace permissions. Your workspace administrator may need to grant access.
2. Enter the KrabiClaw connection details
Use:

Name: KrabiClaw
Description: Manage your KrabiClaw website
MCP server URL / Connection: https://krabiclaw.com/api/mcp
Authentication: OAuth

Copy the exact HTTPS server URL into the connection field. Do not substitute your business's public website domain.
3. Authorize and finish creating the app
Follow the displayed tool-scan and creation flow. When prompted, sign in to the KrabiClaw account that has access to your business and review the requested access before approving it.
Only connect a server you trust. The connection can make real changes to content your account is authorized to manage.
4. Start a new chat and select KrabiClaw
Select the connected app from the available tools or mention it in a new chat. Custom MCP app support and available surfaces follow OpenAI's current requirements; do not assume a developer-created app will work in the mobile app.
Check the connection without changing anything
Ask these separately:

“Which KrabiClaw tools are available in this chat?”
“Which businesses can I manage with KrabiClaw?”
“Show me the current pages for [my business]. Do not change anything.”

The first checks the loaded tool catalog. The next two check access to your account and business. Seeing tools does not prove that the correct business is connected.
If you manage several businesses, choose one explicitly before making any edits.
What the connection can do
The connection operates within your KrabiClaw membership and the tools available in the chat. Supported actions include editing existing-site content, products, media, existing locations, and manually authored language variants, plus drafting and publishing posts to selected destinations.
Reviews, Q&A, contact inquiries, and table-reservation inquiries are available for reading. The connection does not provide review replies, Q&A writing, inquiry replies/status changes, or managed-service work requests.
Site/location creation, domain setup, billing, team management, personal notification settings, and account connections need the dashboard. See What AI assistants can and cannot do before planning a workflow.
Troubleshooting
The MCP server address opens this help page
That is expected when the URL is opened as a normal browser page. Browser requests for HTML at https://krabiclaw.com/api/mcp redirect to this setup guide. Paste the endpoint into the MCP connection field; opening it in a browser does not install the connection.
ChatGPT cannot connect
Check the exact URL, HTTPS, and accidental spaces. Confirm that you completed the OAuth sign-in and that the KrabiClaw account is the one with access to your business.
I cannot find Developer mode or Create app
Check the route, plan, and workspace permissions in OpenAI's linked guidance. Switching devices alone does not grant developer access. If you were given a Personal-plugin installation route, use that route instead of creating a custom app.
New KrabiClaw tools are missing
Start a completely new chat with KrabiClaw selected. For the tested approval-period Personal-plugin flow, use the reinstall and tool-check guide. Confirm you have a way to reinstall before uninstalling. Refresh tools alone did not update the catalog in that tested flow.
The tools appear, but my business is missing
Check which KrabiClaw account authorized the connection and whether your team invitation has been accepted. Business access and tool availability are separate checks.
Next step
Ask KrabiClaw to read one existing page and suggest a small improvement. Review the wording, request the specific edit, and open the public page to verify it.
Use the Personal-plugin installation route provided to you, or use developer-mode custom-app setup if your ChatGPT account and workspace permit it. Search Docs⌘KGetting StartedStart hereCreate your KrabiClaw accountCreate and publish your first sitePrepare your site with ChatGPT, then create it in KrabiClawBuild & EditMake your first site editCustomize your brand and themeAdd photos and videoUpdate locations and hoursRun Your BusinessHandle inquiries and reservation requestsSet up notificationsPublish a postConnect Facebook to KrabiClawConnect Instagram to KrabiClawRead your site analyticsConnect Google Analytics and Search ConsoleAI AssistantsConnect KrabiClaw to ChatGPTWhat AI assistants can and cannot doGet the latest KrabiClaw tools in ChatGPTAccount & SettingsInvite your teamConnect your accounts to KrabiClawDocsAccount & SettingsInvite your teamInvite an Admin or Owner, check pending invitations, and manage organization-wide team access in KrabiClaw.KUpdated Sep 30, 2026·3 min readInvite teammates from your organization's Team → Members page. Current invitations offer Admin and, when you are an Owner, Owner.
Both roles have organization-wide access. Review the recipient and role before sending an invitation.
1. Open the correct organization's Members page
In the dashboard, select the business you want to share, then open Team → Members. The address follows /dashboard/{your-org}/settings/members.
Check the existing team before inviting someone. Use an account with Owner or Admin access.
2. Choose the role

Admin: can manage content, locations, media, products, settings, integrations, and routine business operations across the organization. Admins can invite and manage non-owner teammates. They can read billing information but do not have permission to change billing.
Owner: has organization-wide management access, including billing changes. Only an existing Owner can grant the Owner role or change another Owner's role.

The invitation form does not offer a Member role or a location-only role. Admin is a substantial access grant, not a content-only role.
3. Send the invitation
Choose Invite a team member, enter the person's email address, choose the role, and select Send invite.
Ask the recipient to open the invitation and complete acceptance with the intended account. Sending an invite alone does not mean they have joined.
4. Check acceptance
Return to Members:

Pending Invitations shows invites that have not been accepted, with their expiry dates.
Team shows people who have access and their current role.

If an invitation is no longer useful, cancel it from Pending Invitations. If it has expired, send a new invitation and ask the recipient to use the new one.
Change or remove access
An Owner can use the role selector to change an Admin to Owner or an Owner to Admin. The system prevents the last Owner from demoting themselves, so keep an Owner in place.
For a non-owner teammate, use the remove action beside their name and check that they no longer appear in Team. The list does not offer that removal action for an Owner. An existing Owner must handle any necessary role change first.
If a change fails, read the error and refresh the list before trying again. Do not assume access changed until the updated membership is visible.
Common questions
Why can I only invite an Admin?
Only an existing Owner is offered the Owner invitation option. Ask an Owner if the person genuinely needs that level of access.
Can I limit this person to one branch?
The current Owner and Admin roles apply across the organization. Do not use either role expecting location-only access.
Will new teammates receive my notifications?
Each person controls their own notification categories and channels. WhatsApp delivery uses their own verified phone, not yours.
Next step
Ask each teammate to set up their notification preferences.
